tools.name: searxng_web_search
tools.description: Searches the web using SearXNG and returns a list of results, each with a title, URL, and content snippet. CRITICAL: The required parameter name is exactly `query` (not `prompt`, `q`, or any other name). Calls an external SearXNG instance; availability depends on the `SEARXNG_URL` configuration. Use `pageno` to paginate results; combine `time_range` and `language` to narrow scope. When `engines` and `time_range` are both provided, every selected engine must explicitly advertise time-range support via SearXNG /config; otherwise the request is rejected before search. To read the full text of a result URL, follow up with `web_url_read`.

query.description: The search query string. This is the required parameter name — use exactly `query`, not `prompt` or `q`.

pages.description: Fetch 1 to 5 consecutive pages concurrently starting at pageno; merge and deduplicate before applying the result limit. Failed pages are reported in failedPages in JSON output.

time_range.description: Time range of search (day, week, month, year). With explicit engines, all selected engines must confirm time_range_support=true via /config.

language.description: Language code for search results (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de'). Default is instance-dependent.

safesearch.description: Safe search filter level (0: None, 1: Moderate, 2: Strict)

min_score.description: Minimum relevance score threshold from 0.0 to 1.0. Results below this score are filtered out.

num_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-20). Operator cap SEARXNG_MAX_RESULTS applies as a ceiling.

categories.description: Comma-separated SearXNG categories. Live /config capabilities are aggregated across reachable instances; prefer searxng_instance_info categories.common for consistent multi-instance results. Values in categories.available are best-effort and may only be honored by some instances. Known values are normalized case-insensitively; unknown values are forwarded trimmed so SearXNG can ignore or honor them. If /config is unavailable, values are forwarded as-is with a warning. If omitted, each instance uses its server-side default.

engines.description: Comma-separated SearXNG engine names to query (e.g. 'google,bing,ddg'). Live /config capabilities are aggregated across reachable instances; prefer searxng_instance_info engines.common.enabled for consistent multi-instance results. Values in engines.available.enabled are best-effort and may only be honored by some instances. Known values are normalized case-insensitively; unknown values are forwarded trimmed so SearXNG can ignore or honor them. If /config is unavailable, values are forwarded as-is with a warning. If omitted, each instance uses its server-side default.

response_format.description: Response format: formatted text for agents or raw JSON for programmatic clients. If omitted, SEARXNG_DEFAULT_RESPONSE_FORMAT applies; if unset or invalid, text is used. An explicit response_format always takes precedence.

result_detail.description: Result detail: full preserves SearXNG metadata and search signals; compact returns only title, URL, and content-snippet fields for each result (JSON keys: title, url, content). If omitted, full is used.

tools.poisoning_detail: Steering language in tool description (imperative guidance aimed at the model). Matched pattern in tool 'searxng_web_search': 'always'

tools.name: searxng_search_suggestions
tools.description: Returns autocomplete suggestions from the configured SearXNG instance. Use this to refine vague or partial queries before searching.

query.description: Partial or complete query to autocomplete.

language.description: Language code for suggestions (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de') or 'all'. Default: all.

tools.name: searxng_instance_info
tools.description: Discovers capabilities from all reachable configured SearXNG instances via /config, including categories.common/available, engines.common/available, defaults, locales, and plugins.

includeEngines.description: Include enabled engine names in the response.

includeDisabled.description: Include disabled engine names when includeEngines is true.

category.description: Filter categories and engines to a single category name.

refresh.description: Bypass the process cache and fetch fresh /config data.

tools.name: web_url_read
tools.description: Fetch URL. Converts HTML to markdown; returns explicit JSON, plain text, YAML, TOML, and XML as readable markdown; supports bounded PDF text extraction; other binary/media/archive downloads are rejected. When browser solvers are configured, mcp-searxng attempts FlareSolverr first and then Byparr only after a busy or transient-unavailable acquisition; after a final busy or unavailable provider it uses one uncached direct read.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
